title: personal-okr-weekly-checkin-avery-chen-2026-04-15
content:
Week of 2026-04-15 — Personal OKR / weekly check-in (working notes)

Quick context (for manager/skip):
- Q2 focus aligned to eng-serving-runtime OKRs: reduce p95 tail latency, improve throughput for 8k+ seq workloads, and ship the KV cache safety checks.
- Personal goals: 1) Lead rollout of async batching feature (perf + stability) 2) Mentor two new ICs and improve on-call runbook 3) Reduce client-facing incidents by 25% versus Q1 baseline.

Accomplishments this week:
- Async batching: merged core runtime changes (PR 234) and validated on staging with synthetic traffic. Observed 18% CPU reduction for 4k seq scenarios and 12% lower tail latency in regression tests.
- KV cache safety checks: final design doc posted to Confluence for review (CONFLUENCE-ENG-3572). Basic integration tests implemented.
- Mentoring: 1:1 with Priya scheduled twice; helped debug her first integration test failure for the memory leak issue.
- On-call: led postmortem write-up for incident on 2026-04-12 (JIRA-ENG-7891) and proposed a short-term mitigation (circuit-breaker on long-running requests).

Metrics / KR progress (numbers approximate, baseline = end of Q1):
- KR1: Reduce cluster-level p95 latency for text-generation by 20% — current delta: ~15% (on track, need another 5% improvement).
- KR2: Increase effective throughput for long sequences (>=4k): target 2x; current measured: 1.6x vs baseline.
- KR3: On-call incidents impacting customers reduced by 25% — observed reduction 18% so far.

Notes / observations:
- Staging perf looks promising, but the production-like traffic shape (bursty prefixes) still causes occasional KV cache thrashing. Need to tune TTL heuristics and preheat logic.
- Async batching exposes some edge cases with backpressure; saw a backlog spike when small-request traffic suddenly increased. Likely due to thresholding heuristics in the frontend router.
- Need better telemetry around request grouping decisions to debug later regressions (add logs + sampling traces).

Blockers / help needed:
- Product asked for a compatibility check with the new model quantization profile by EOD Tue — I need a quick set of perf runs on dedicated-dev farm. Can infra grant access to 2x A100 nodes for 4 hours? (cc Hunter)
- Need review on the KV cache safety PR (link above); two LGTMs required from SRE and runtime. Jamie, can you help nudge?

Plan for next week:
- Rollout plan: canary async batching on 10% traffic, measure p95 and error rate over 48h windows. Coordinate with rollout team and SRE.
- Telemetry: add sampling traces for batch formation (trace_id + batch_id) and emit histogram for batch size distribution.
- Mentoring: pair with Priya on integration tests; get her to own the follow-up memory leak fix.
- Docs: finalize runbook updates for on-call (short-term mitigation + long-term fix timeline).

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: rollout exposes additional tail latency for small requests when batching delay increases. Mitigation: implement fast-path bypass for requests flagged latency-sensitive (heuristic flag for low-latency routes).
- Risk: KV cache preheat could increase memory pressure. Mitigation: adaptive preheat with soft quotas + evict-by-age policy.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Request infra access for perf runs (submit infra ticket) — owner: Avery — due: 2026-04-17
- [ ] Ping SRE for KV cache safety PR review — owner: Jamie — due: 2026-04-16
- [ ] Add batch telemetry + sampling traces — owner: Avery/Priya — due: 2026-04-20
- [ ] Draft canary rollout checklist and notify product & support — owner: Avery — due: 2026-04-19

Retrospective quick notes (personal):
- I did well pushing the staging runs earlier, but could have escalated to infra sooner when jobs queued up — reduce friction by pre-booking slots next sprint.
- Mentoring: need to give more explicit test-writing examples during pairing (tendency to talk through approach rather than live-coding).

Random thoughts / scratchpad:
- Might be worth a small eval: run a synthetic with mixed short+long requests to tune batching thresholds automatically (learning-based threshold?).
- Consider a short RFC for "latency-sensitive route annotation" that product can opt into for critical user flows.
- Follow-up: sync with Hunter on autoscale policy tweaks for dedicated (to avoid burst pressure).

Links / refs:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-ENG-3572 (KV cache safety checks design)
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-7891 (incident 2026-04-12 postmortem)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/234 (async batching merge)


Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight — copy to the weekly check-in form on Monday.
